newsitem.title: USA: Hanson Energy sees U.S. merger activity.
newsitem.headline: Hanson Energy sees U.S. merger activity.

text.p: Energy Group Plc intends to participate in U.S. utility mergers, chief executive Derek Bonham told security analysts Monday.

Deregulation of U.S. utilities is "creating an unprecedented level of merger and acquisition activity in the sector," he noted at the first of a series of meetings on the company's pending spin-off from Hanson Plc.
"We intend to participate" using the company's Peabody coal company as a base, Bonham said.
This will "not necessarily (mean) putting out the big bucks," he cautioned.
Energy Group is interested in getting access to power generation rather than owning generating assets, Bonham said.
The spin-off is on schedule for the planned February 21 vote of Hanson shareholders, he said.
This is expected to result in Energy Group's stock and ADRs beginning trading February 24, on the London and New York stock exchanges, respectively, he said.
Bonham said said he does not expect the stock to have a premium like Enron Corp's "out of the box," explaining he sees it priced more like a traditional utility initially.
Finance Director Eric Anstee said Energy Group expects ongoing capital spending for the next few years to fall in the 200 to 250 million stg range.
That is down from the 370 million stg spent in the year ended September 30, he said, pointing out the 1996 total included 92 million for acquisitions.

This year's planned spending includes about 120 million stg for the company's power distribution networks in England and 90 million for Peabody Holding Co Inc subsidiary, which mines coal in the U.S. and Australia, Anstee said.

He said Energy Group intends to invest the cash flows generated by Peabody and its distribution networks in power projects. But he declined to respond to analysts questions about what spending was planned in this area.
Noting the company is starting with a debt coverage ratio of 5, Anstee said he does not see it declining below 3.5 on any merger transaction.
Bonham responded to questions about expected earnings growth by referring to the information statement on the proposed spin-off.

In particular, he noted the statement's expectation that the dividend for the year ended September 30 would have been 21 pence based on proforma results and this had risen to 22 pence a year based on expected results through March 30.
Putting the six month change in expectations on an annual basis results in an increase of 5 percent, he said, explaining both are based on an expected payout ratio of about 42 percent.

Bonham also noted an all or nothing bonus being offered to senior management if earnings increase 6 percent in addition to inflation. This would be a two year increase of about 10 percent, he said. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
